Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: richly detailed miniature city concept art for the existing early twentieth-century military city-building strategy game's world map.
Style: premium semi-realistic 3D diorama, beautifully art-directed architectural scale model, tactile stone, plaster, slate, painted metal and foliage. Strong three-dimensional form, beveled edges, convincing building thickness, roof overhangs, layered heights, carefully controlled ambient occlusion and soft cast shadows. Sophisticated strategy-game art, not a flat icon.
Composition: one complete coherent city on one shallow square landscaped terrain base, elevated isometric three-quarter camera at approximately 35 degrees, orthographic feel, square composition, entire model visible with 10 percent clear margin. About 16-24 buildings grouped into legible districts, dominant landmark and balanced subordinate structures. Roads connect logically. Rich details reward zooming in while large masses form a readable small silhouette. No collage or multiple views.
Lighting: beautiful soft daylight from upper left with subtle warm highlights, cool soft shadows, crisp all-in-focus miniature photography, no depth-of-field blur.
Palette: desaturated slate blue roofs, warm gray limestone and cream plaster, restrained brick accents, olive and sage vegetation compatible with a light sage green game map and blue-gray UI. Pale warm gray seamless studio background, subtle grounding shadow.
Constraints: period-appropriate 1930s-1940s architecture and infrastructure. No modern skyscrapers, science fiction, fantasy castles, neon colors, giant signage, readable text, logos, watermarks or political insignia. No battle damage or smoky atmosphere obscuring the city. No giant objects or trees taller than the landmark. Refined and attractive, dense but thoughtfully composed.

City design: a prosperous inland administrative and military capital. Central imposing neoclassical stone headquarters with a columned entrance, broad steps, symmetrical wings and a distinctive restrained clock tower; a formal plaza and small circular fountain. Around it: lovely townhouse blocks with varied pitched slate roofs and dormers, civic offices, market arcades, a post office, two tidy barracks, supply warehouses near the edge, a small park with mature trees and flower beds. Cobblestone streets, sidewalks, lamps, low fences, tiny period delivery trucks, roof chimneys and courtyard details. The headquarters remains clearly dominant. Warm, elegant, believable inhabited city.

City design: a compact fortified military city with civilian neighborhoods. A substantial early twentieth-century masonry command headquarters and communications tower sit on a slightly raised central terrace. Low angular concrete perimeter defenses, practical fortified gates and small observation towers, not medieval castle crenellations. Attractive layered terraces and clear architectural hierarchy; a richly inhabited strategic stronghold, no combat.

Along one edge of the square terrain base: a narrow jewel-like muted teal harbor basin with visible quay depth, stone seawall, two period dock cranes, cargo warehouses, a small lighthouse, two small moored civilian cargo vessels, bollards, ropes and neatly stacked cargo.
